page: Amazon Web Services m7i.12xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance in several areas, particularly in cryptographic and vector-based operations. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to strong scores in Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests. Single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench multi-core performance are also strong. In terms of memory performance, the DDR5 configuration achieves an average read-only small block bandwidth of 3571.17 GB/sec, though large-block uncached write bandwidth is more moderate at 84.16 GB/sec.

This instance is well-suited for workloads requiring balanced compute and memory resources without the need for local NVMe storage. Strong database operations and Redis SET performance of 63.12 million operations per second make it highly capable for caching layers and relational databases. Additionally, the inclusion of AMX instructions enables strong performance in small-to-medium LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation, without requiring expensive GPU resources.

It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps. The processor's support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) enables efficient low-latency LLM inference for small and medium models. This instance is optimized for workloads such as database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from high-speed DDR5 memory and dedicated compute resources without requiring local SSD storage.
